Super cool movie. It was like an action movie version of "Honey, I Shrunk the Kids". I got a kick out of the Avengers tie ins, too.

Also, Evangeline Lily.

The fight scenes were creative enough to keep a jaded super hero movie goer excited. The appeal was Paul Rudd's ability to pay the character which he did pretty well. If you're interested in a super hero movie that's different from the norm, spend your money to watch this one.

We as a culture tend to be of the opinion that "we're sick of origin stories." The Nolan Bat films are barely cold in the grave, and already we are traipsing out Bat Afleck, who will have his origins explained yet again. We all know what happened, but for the sake of storytelling we'll be seeing a few scenes going over it.

Spider-man will likely receive similar treatment in Civil War.

I mention all this, because I feel, in the same vein as Guardians of the Galaxy, the relatively unknown Ant-Man's origin felt like a much needed refresher to the MCU. They acknowledge the weirdness of it all, they embrace how strange the ideas presented seem, and they showcase exactly how cool it can be. Ant-Man is trained in the ways of the suit, and adapts to the power quickly. Paul Rudd pulls off the title role well, Micheal Douglas is eccentric, and Neon Genesis Evangeline Lilly is cool, but rude.

It has a few of the classic Marvel film moments that make you roll your eyes, but overall it holds up well.
